prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production pixel sprite proposal sheet for Teamfight Manager 2. Use image 1 only for character identity/clothing; image 2 only for the approved simple blocky low-resolution game style. Draw new silhouettes, not a recolour or photographic render. Exactly eight full-body key poses in a strict 4-column x 2-row grid, landscape 1536x1024; each pose comfortably inside its own 384x512 cell with generous transparent margins and no overlap. All poses face right at a slight three-quarter game angle; consistent camera, anatomy and scale. A deliberately coarse pixel grid: each sprite should look designed at roughly 40–46 visible pixels tall then enlarged with nearest-neighbour pixels; compact blocky masses, firm dark outlines, 2 or 3 flat shades, no texture noise, no dithering, no soft gradients, no anti-aliasing. Actual alpha-transparent background, no ground shadows or glows, no grid lines, no captions or text. Keep the feet on a consistent baseline per row. Sheet is appearance approval material, not a final game atlas. Subject: Darth Vader, classic original-trilogy suit. Recognizable flared domed black helmet with triangular mouth grille and dark lenses, broad charcoal shoulder armour, ribbed black bodysuit, long black cape with legible slate-grey interior folds, small chest controls and belt boxes with restrained red/blue/ivory pixels, black boots, red lightsaber with a thin white-hot core. Keep clear black shapes readable on dark terrain. NO hood, no exposed face, no medieval armour, no huge helmet, no generic knight. The body should be about the height of the style character or slightly taller; the cape is his silhouette. Poses in reading order: 1 composed idle holding saber down-right, 2 deliberate walking stride cape trailing, 3 horizontal saber cut, 4 raised saber follow-through, 5 free hand Force-push extension with saber lowered, 6 pinching Force-choke hand gesture, 7 two-handed commanding raised pose for ultimate, 8 hit recoil while keeping helmet/cape identity. Saber and hands fully contained in the cells.
